3.meaning: A question particle ('is...?') joined to the preposition meaning 'in/about/concerning'. Together they open an interrogative that asks whether something exists 'in' or 'about' a matter.
3.grammar: The opening 'a-' is the interrogative prefix that turns a statement into a yes/no question. 'fī' is a preposition meaning 'in/within/about'; it governs a following noun in the genitive case.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: Doubt, uncertainty, or suspicion; a wavering of the mind between two possibilities, the opposite of sure conviction.
5.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks the nominative case and signals indefiniteness ('a doubt / any doubt'); the nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing whose existence is being asserted or questioned.
5.root: ش-ك-ك (sh-k-k) — doubt, uncertainty

6.meaning: 'Originator', 'Bringer-into-being', 'Maker who splits forth creation from nothing'. The word names the one who first brings things into existence, cleaving them into being where there was none.

parts.en: originator / one who brings into being

6.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun: 'the one who originates'). The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically links the word to a following noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. As a doer-noun it can also take an object after it.
6.root: ف-ط-ر (f-ṭ-r) — to split, cleave, bring forth, originate

7.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
7.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

8.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
8.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

9.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he calls / summons / invites you (plural)' — to call out to someone, beckoning or summoning them.
9.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The ya- prefix marks 'he'; the verb ends in the weak long vowel -ū of its root. The attached -kum is the direct object 'you all'.
9.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, supplicate

10.meaning: 'so that He may forgive' — to forgive, to cover over and pardon a wrong so that it is not held against the person.
10.grammar: The purpose-particle li- ('so that, in order to') joined to a present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He forgives'). Because of li-, the verb is subjunctive, shown by the final -a ending, which gives the sense of intended result: 'so that He may forgive'.
10.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield; to forgive, pardon

11.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
11.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

12.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
12.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

13.meaning: Sins, wrongdoings, faults; offenses attributed to a 'your (plural)' possessor.
13.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, 'sins', with the attached pronoun '-kum' = 'your' (for a group). The '-i' ending is genitive: it appears because the noun is possessed ('the sins OF you') and also occurs after a preposition.
13.root: ذ-ن-ب (dh-n-b) — sin, fault, offense

14.meaning: 'And He defers/postpones you' — to grant a delay or reprieve, putting off an appointed term to a later time.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive (form II) pattern, 'he defers/grants delay', with 'he' shown by the 'yu-' prefix and '-kum' = 'you all' as its object. The '-a' ending is the subjunctive, used after certain particles (such as 'so that' or a linking 'and') to express purpose or a connected result.
14.root: ا-خ-ر ('-kh-r) — to be last, to delay, to put off

15.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
15.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

16.meaning: A noun meaning 'a fixed term, an appointed time, a set deadline, a span allotted before something falls due.' It denotes the limit or end-point of a period.
16.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a term'). This form occurs after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun.
16.root: ا-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed time, deadline

17.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'named, specified, designated, made definite.' It describes something that has been clearly stated and fixed by name — a term that is precisely set rather than vague.
17.grammar: A passive participle (the mu- prefix forms a 'one that is …' word from the Form II intensive pattern, with a doubled middle root letter) meaning 'named/specified.' It carries the indefinite ending -an, written with alif maqṣūra (a final ya-shaped letter sounded as -ā). Because it ends in this weak final letter, the form stays the same whether nominative, accusative, or genitive — context shows it is describing an indefinite noun.
17.root: س-م-ي (s-m-y) — name, naming; to give or assign a name

18.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

19.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
19.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

20.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
20.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

21.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
21.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

22.meaning: 'A human being, a mortal man' — bashar denotes humankind as flesh-and-blood mortals. It emphasizes the human, bodily nature of a person.
22.grammar: A noun (also usable collectively for 'mankind'). The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a human being'). The nominative case marks it as the subject of a sentence (e.g. the one who acts) or as a noun whose existence is being affirmed or denied.

23.meaning: Like us; similar to us, of the same kind as us.

parts.en: like / similar to / the equal of

23.grammar: A noun meaning 'a like / equal', with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('us'), giving 'our like = like us'. The '-u' on the stem is the nominative (subject) case ending, used when the word stands as subject or predicate. The attached '-nā' is in the genitive as the possessor.

24.meaning: You (plural) want, intend, desire, or seek — to direct one's will toward something and aim at it.
24.grammar: A present-tense verb in the 'you all' form. The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject and signals the causative (form-IV) pattern; the suffix -ūna combines the masculine-plural subject ('you all') with the indicative mood — the kept final -na shows a plain statement (not a command or subjunctive, where that -na would drop).
24.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to go to and fro after something; will, intention

25.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
25.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

26.meaning: 'You (plural) turn us away / bar us / hinder us' — to block or divert someone from a path or intention.
26.grammar: A present-tense form I verb built on a geminate (doubled) root, 'to turn (someone) away / hinder'; the two identical final root letters merge, which is why the consonant appears doubled (with shaddah). The 'ta-...-ū' frame marks a masculine plural 'you' subject, and '-nā' = 'us' is the object. Because the long-vowel ending '-ū' is retained (rather than dropped), the verb is in its base indicative form, stating an ongoing or general action.
26.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, avert, hinder

27.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
27.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

28.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

28.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

29.meaning: "he worships / he serves devotedly" — the present-tense act of worship by a single "he" subject.
29.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a single masculine "he" subject; the final -u is the indicative present, expressing an ongoing, habitual, or general action.

30.meaning: Our fathers and forefathers; our ancestors. The word points to the line of male forebears whose example or tradition is often invoked.
30.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our') attached. The plural ends in a hamza (written here on a 'wāw' seat as 'ؤ'), and the '-u' vowel on it before the pronoun is nominative, the case typically used when the noun is the subject (the doer) of a sentence.

31.meaning: 'So bring us / come to us (with) …' — a command addressed to a group to produce or bring forth something.
31.grammar: A command (imperative) verb from the root meaning 'to come / bring', addressed to a plural 'you' (shown by '-ū'), with '-nā' = 'us' as the object. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'so/then', linking the command as a consequence of what came before.

32.meaning: An authority, a sanction, a compelling proof or warrant — that which gives one power or a decisive basis to act or argue; combined with 'with / by.'
32.grammar: A masculine noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with / by means of'). The -in ending is the genitive with tanwīn (doubled kasra), which is the case required after a preposition; the tanwīn marks the noun indefinite ('with an authority / a proof').
32.root: س-ل-ط (s-l-ṭ) — power, dominion, sanction; a decisive proof that empowers

33.meaning: Means 'clear / plain / making manifest' — something that is evident in itself and also makes other things plain, leaving no ambiguity.
33.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) from a pattern that often carries the sense 'making clear' as well as 'being clear.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite), the form taken after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun — i.e. it agrees with a preceding indefinite noun in the genitive ('a clear …').
33.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make evident

1.meaning: She said — a completed act of speaking or saying, attributed to a single female.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -at ending that marks a single female doer ('she said'). The plain past form presents the action as a completed whole.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: Their messengers — the envoys or apostles sent by Allah, here belonging to 'them'; 'rusul' is the plural of 'rasūl', one who is dispatched bearing a message.
3.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -hum ending means 'their' (for a group of males). The -u vowel before it is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a sentence.
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger, an envoy

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: The detached pronoun 'we' — standing alone to name or emphasize the speakers as a group ('we ourselves').
5.grammar: An independent (standalone) personal pronoun meaning 'we'. Such detached pronouns are not inflected for case; they serve as the subject of a sentence or add emphasis ('it is we who…'). The fixed final '-u' is simply part of the pronoun's form. (The doubling shown on the opening nūn reflects assimilation in connected recitation with a preceding word, not a change in the pronoun itself.)

6.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
6.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

7.meaning: 'A human being, a mortal man' — bashar denotes humankind as flesh-and-blood mortals. It emphasizes the human, bodily nature of a person.
7.grammar: A noun (also usable collectively for 'mankind'). The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a human being'). The nominative case marks it as the subject of a sentence (e.g. the one who acts) or as a noun whose existence is being affirmed or denied.

8.meaning: One like you, your equal, of the same kind as you (addressing a group) — 'a like' or 'counterpart' joined to the plural 'you'. It asserts sameness of nature.
8.grammar: The noun mithl ('like, equal') with the attached pronoun -kum ('you', addressing a group of males or a mixed group). The -u ending is nominative, typically marking the word as the subject or as a predicate ('… is one like you').
8.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, resemblance; a match or equal

9.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
9.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.
9.root: — (particle)

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: 'He bestows a favour / shows grace' — to grant a kindness freely; the same root can also mean to follow a gift with reminders of it.
11.grammar: A present-tense form I verb built on a geminate (doubled) root, 'he bestows a favour / shows grace', with 'he' marked by the 'ya-' prefix; the doubled final consonant (shaddah) results from the two identical root letters merging. The final '-u' vowel marks the indicative mood, stating a present or habitual action ('he grants').
11.root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n) — to bestow a favour, to be gracious

12.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
12.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

13.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
13.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
13.root: — (pronoun)

14.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
14.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

16.meaning: 'His servants / His slaves / His worshippers' — ʿibād are those who serve and worship; with the attached pronoun it denotes the servants belonging to Him (Allah), i.e., humankind or His devotees.
16.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel is the genitive case, typically appearing after a preposition or in a possessive ('of') link; the pronoun names the one to whom the servants belong.

17.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
17.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

18.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

18.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

19.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
19.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

20.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
20.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

21.meaning: '(That) we bring you / come to you with …' — to produce or present something to a group of people.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb from 'to come/bring', with the 'na-' prefix marking a 'we' subject and '-kum' = 'you all' as the object. The '-a' ending is subjunctive, used after particles of purpose or possibility ('so that we may bring you'). (The doubling shown on the prefix nūn reflects assimilation with a preceding word in connected recitation.)

22.meaning: An authority, a sanction, a compelling proof or warrant — that which gives one power or a decisive basis to act or argue; combined with 'with / by.'
22.grammar: A masculine noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with / by means of'). The -in ending is the genitive with tanwīn (doubled kasra), which is the case required after a preposition; the tanwīn marks the noun indefinite ('with an authority / a proof').
22.root: س-ل-ط (s-l-ṭ) — power, dominion, sanction; a decisive proof that empowers

23.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
23.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

24.meaning: 'By the leave of / with the permission of' — formed from 'with/by' plus 'permission, leave, sanction'. It conveys that something happens by someone's authorization or enabling will.
24.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition 'with/by'. The noun 'idhn' means 'permission, leave, sanction'. After the preposition it takes the genitive -i ending, the form used following a preposition and typically linking on to a following noun ('the permission OF …').
24.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; also listening/ear

25.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
25.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

26.meaning: A two-part phrase: the joining word 'and' plus the preposition 'on / upon / incumbent upon,' often used to express an obligation resting on someone.
26.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') joined to the preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon'). Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending; a noun governed by 'ʿalā' takes the genitive.

27.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
27.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

28.meaning: An exhortation: 'so let (someone) put their trust' — to place complete reliance and dependence (tawakkul) upon Allah, committing one's affairs to Him.
28.grammar: A third-person command (jussive of command). 'fa-' connects ('so'), the prefixed 'li-' turns the verb into an order ('let him…'), and 'ya-' marks a third-person 'he' subject. The final '-i' is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before the next word, not a case ending.
28.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, rely, commit one's affairs

29.meaning: The believers — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm the truth and give it their security and assent.
29.grammar: A definite noun, the active participle of form IV ('mu'min,' 'one who believes/grants security'). The plural ending '-ūna' marks a masculine human plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or doer ('the believers' as those performing the action).

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
1.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

2.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
2.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

3.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
3.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

4.meaning: '(That) we rely / put our trust' — to commit one's affairs and dependence wholly to another, especially to Allah.
4.grammar: A present-tense reflexive verb (form V) meaning 'to place one's trust / rely', with the 'na-' prefix marking 'we'. The '-a' ending is subjunctive, used after purpose particles like 'so that' to express a reason ('that we should trust').
4.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, to rely upon

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
7.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

8.meaning: 'He guided us' — a past-tense verb of guiding, showing the right way, or leading aright, with the object 'us' attached. The root denotes guidance and right direction.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with a third-person masculine singular subject built into it — 'he.' The long final -ā belongs to a weak-ending root (its last letter is a vowel-like letter). The attached -nā is the object 'us,' so the whole means 'he guided us.'
8.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, to guide, to show the right way

9.meaning: 'Our ways / paths / roads' — courses or routes one travels, here possessed by 'us'; figuratively, the manner or course of conduct.
9.grammar: A plural noun, 'ways/paths', with '-nā' = 'our' attached. The '-a' ending marks the accusative case, which commonly identifies the object of a verb or otherwise signals a noun that is acted upon or specified.
9.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

10.meaning: An emphatic pledge: 'and we shall most certainly endure with patience' — to bear hardship steadfastly without complaint.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to be patient/endure', with 'na-' marking 'we'. The combination of the prefixed 'la-' ('surely') and the heavy suffix '-anna' forms a strong oath-like emphasis, turning the verb into a firm promise: 'we will most certainly endure'.

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

12.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

13.meaning: 'You (plural) have harmed/hurt us' — to inflict injury, offense, or annoyance upon someone.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb 'to harm/injure'. The suffix '-tum' marks a masculine plural 'you' as the doer, lengthened to '-tumū' to join the following object '-nā' = 'us'. Past-tense verbs carry their subject in the ending rather than a prefix.
13.root: ا-ذ-ي ('-dh-y) — to harm, hurt, cause injury

14.meaning: A two-part phrase: the joining word 'and' plus the preposition 'on / upon / incumbent upon,' often used to express an obligation resting on someone.
14.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') joined to the preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon'). Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending; a noun governed by 'ʿalā' takes the genitive.

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: An exhortation: 'so let (someone) put their trust' — to place complete reliance and dependence (tawakkul) upon Allah, committing one's affairs to Him.
16.grammar: A third-person command (jussive of command). 'fa-' connects ('so'), the prefixed 'li-' turns the verb into an order ('let him…'), and 'ya-' marks a third-person 'he' subject. The final '-i' is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before the next word, not a case ending.
16.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, rely, commit one's affairs

17.meaning: 'The ones who place their trust / the reliant ones' — those who consistently entrust their affairs and dependence to Allah.
17.grammar: An active participle (form V) naming the doer, 'one who relies/trusts', made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The '-ūna' ending is the masculine sound plural in the nominative case, typically marking the subject or a noun being described ('those who trust').
17.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, to rely upon

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: 'To / for their messengers' — those sent with a message; envoys or apostles, possessed by 'them'.
4.grammar: A plural noun, 'messengers', preceded by the preposition 'li-' ('to/for') and followed by '-him' = 'their'. The '-i' ending is genitive, required both by the preceding preposition and by the possessive attachment ('the messengers OF them').
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger, envoy

5.meaning: An emphatic threat: 'we shall most certainly drive you out / expel you' — to force someone to leave a place.
5.grammar: A present-tense causative verb (form IV) 'to expel/drive out', with 'nu-' marking 'we' and '-kum' = 'you all' as the object. The prefixed 'la-' ('surely') together with the heavy '-anna' forms an emphatic vow: 'we will assuredly expel you'.
5.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out; (form IV) to bring/drive out

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

7.meaning: 'Our land / earth / territory' — the ground or homeland, here belonging to 'us'.
7.grammar: A feminine noun, 'land/earth', with '-nā' = 'our' attached. The '-i' ending is genitive, which here arises from the possessive construction ('the land OF us') and also appears after prepositions.

8.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
8.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

9.meaning: An emphatic statement or oath-bound assertion addressed to one man: 'you shall surely return / go back.' The root means to return, to come back, or to revert to a former state or practice.
9.grammar: A present/future verb with the ta- prefix marking the addressee 'you.' With no plural marker (no wāw) before the ending, the form is second-person masculine singular — a single man. It carries double emphasis: the prefixed la- ('surely') and the heavy emphatic ending -nna, making it a solemn, almost oath-like assertion ('you absolutely will return').
9.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, come back, revert

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: 'Our way / creed / religious path,' joined to a 'we/our' possessor. The base word denotes a defined body of belief and practice — a religious community's followed way.
11.grammar: A feminine noun, 'creed' or 'religious way' (base form milla, ending in ta marbuta). With a possessor attached, the ta marbuta surfaces as a pronounced -t- and takes a linking -i — the construct (iḍāfa) realization of the feminine ending, not a separate case morpheme — followed by -nā ('our'): 'our creed / our way.'
11.root: م-ل-ل (m-l-l) — a followed creed or religious community

12.meaning: 'So He revealed / inspired' — to convey a message swiftly and hiddenly, especially divine revelation cast into a heart or messenger.
12.grammar: A past-tense causative verb (form IV) 'to reveal/inspire'. With no attached subject pronoun, the bare form carries a 'he' subject. The 'fa-' prefix means 'so/then', presenting the action as a consequence of what preceded.
12.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, inspire, communicate secretly

13.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
13.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
13.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

14.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Nurturer who owns, provides, and brings to maturity) joined to the pronoun 'their'.
14.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -u vowel before -hum is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as the subject/doer. The suffix -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine plural group.
14.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

15.meaning: An emphatic divine declaration: 'We shall most certainly destroy / annihilate' — to bring to ruin and cause to perish.
15.grammar: A present-tense causative verb (form IV) 'to destroy/cause to perish', with 'nu-' marking 'we'. The prefixed 'la-' ('surely') and heavy '-anna' suffix combine into a solemn, emphatic promise: 'we will surely destroy'.
15.root: ه-ل-ك (h-l-k) — to perish; (form IV) to destroy

16.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
16.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: An emphatic promise: 'and We shall most certainly settle you / make you dwell' — to cause people to reside and find a dwelling place.
1.grammar: A present-tense causative verb (form IV) 'to cause to dwell/settle', with 'nu-' marking 'we' and '-kum' = 'you all' as the object (its vowel shifted to '-kumu' before a following word). The prefixed 'la-' plus heavy '-anna' make it an emphatic vow: 'we will surely settle you'.
1.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, to dwell, to reside

2.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
2.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'
2.root: أ-ر-ض (ʼ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: "after them / following them" — the noun baʿd ('after, afterward') with the attached pronoun 'them', denoting what comes later in time than a group.
4.grammar: A time-noun used like a preposition, with an attached pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, the form taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive link. The suffix -him means 'them' (its vowel is -hi- to harmonise with the preceding -i).
4.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, what follows

5.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
5.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

6.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
6.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

7.meaning: He feared / was afraid — a completed act of fearing, dreading, or apprehending some harm or danger.
7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) hollow verb (its middle root letter is a long 'ā'). The final '-a' marks third-person masculine singular: "he" did it, viewed as completed.

8.meaning: 'My standing-place / station' — a place or occasion of standing; figuratively one's standing before Allah, here marked as 'mine'.
8.grammar: A noun of place from 'to stand', meaning 'a place/station of standing', with the attached '-ī' = 'my'. When the possessive '-ī' ('my') is attached, it replaces the visible case ending, so the case is understood from context rather than a separate vowel.

9.meaning: 'And he feared / was in awe' — to dread, to hold in reverent fear; an inner alarm before something dangerous or majestic.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb 'to fear'. The final '-a' (fatha) is the ending of the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he feared'); past-tense verbs carry their subject in this ending rather than a prefix. The opening 'wa-' simply means 'and', joining it to what precedes.
9.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — fear, dread, awe

10.meaning: 'My threat / My warning of punishment' — a promise of impending chastisement, here marked as belonging to the speaker ('Mine').
10.grammar: A verbal noun, 'a threat/warning of punishment'. The final '-i' is the genitive case vowel of the noun, the case used after prepositions and in possessive links. The possessive sense ('my') comes from a possessive 'y' (ī, 'my') that is attached but dropped at a pause, leaving only the genitive '-i' visible.
10.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise; (of evil) to threaten

1.meaning: 'And they sought a decisive opening / victory / judgement' — to ask for a clear verdict or for triumph to be granted.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'seeking' pattern (form X), 'to seek an opening/victory/judgement'. The '-ū' ending marks a masculine plural 'they' as the doer (the silent alif after it is only spelling). The 'wa-' prefix means 'and'.
1.root: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open; to grant victory or a decisive judgement

2.meaning: And he/it failed and came to nothing; was thwarted, frustrated, and left disappointed. The verb conveys the bitter outcome of an effort or hope that ends in utter loss and futility.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it did'). The hollow root's middle weak letter surfaces as the long ā. The bare -a ending with no attached subject means the action is complete and the doer is simply 'he' or 'it'. The wa- prefix is the connector 'and'.
2.root: خ-ي-ب (kh-y-b) — failure, frustration, disappointment, coming to nothing

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
3.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.

4.meaning: An intensive noun/adjective meaning 'a tyrant, an overbearing oppressor' — one who is haughty and compels others by force, arrogant and domineering. (The same root word can describe a restorer/mender, but in the human-descriptive sense it denotes overbearing arrogance.)
4.grammar: An intensive noun on the faʿʿāl pattern, denoting one who does something habitually or to a high degree. The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (indefinite); this ending typically appears after a preposition or when the word follows and qualifies another genitive noun.
4.root: ج-ب-ر (j-b-r) — to compel, force; also to set/mend

5.meaning: An adjective meaning 'obstinate, stubbornly defiant' — one who knowingly persists in opposition, turning away from the truth out of sheer contrariness.
5.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (indefinite), the ending normally used when the word follows a preposition or describes a preceding genitive noun.
5.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — to oppose stubbornly, deviate, be obstinate

1.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
1.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

2.meaning: From behind him / before him; on the far side of him. A spatial term built on a noun meaning 'the rear' or 'what lies beyond,' joined to a possessive 'his.' Idiomatically it can point either to what is behind a person or to what lies ahead awaiting him.
2.grammar: A noun of place meaning 'behind/beyond,' carrying the -i genitive ending because it is bound to the following possessor (literally 'the-behind OF him'). The attached -hi means 'his/him'; its vowel is -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows the -i sound. The wa- prefix is 'and.'
2.root: و-ر-ي (w-r-y) — to be behind, hidden, or beyond; the rear side

3.meaning: Hell / Jahannam — the proper name of the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter.
3.grammar: A proper name (the name of Hell), treated as a feminine, non-fully-inflecting noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, marking it as the subject/predicate of a statement ('… is Jahannam'). Because it is a proper name of this type, it does not take the usual final '-n' (tanwīn) of ordinary nouns.

4.meaning: And he is given to drink; he is made to drink. A passive verb describing someone who does not drink by choice but is caused to swallow some liquid, the act being imposed upon him.
4.grammar: A present/future passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('he is being / will be made to drink'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks it as passive ('is done to him' rather than 'he does'), and the final weak letter appears as the long ā. The wa- prefix is 'and.'
4.root: س-ق-ي (s-q-y) — to give to drink, to water, to irrigate

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: Water, the life-giving fluid; rain or any liquid that sustains.
6.grammar: An indefinite singular noun ('water / some water'). The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and is the genitive case form, taken after a preposition or when a noun follows another in an 'of' relationship.

7.meaning: Pus, festering matter, foul discharge that oozes from a wound or sore; by extension a vile, putrid fluid. The word names a thick, repugnant liquid associated with corruption and decay.
7.grammar: A singular noun carrying the tanwīn ending written with a kasra (-in), marking it as indefinite ('some pus / pus'). Although the vowel is a kasra, the noun functions as the substitute-subject (the thing actually given to drink) of a passive verb, so its grammatical case is nominative, not genitive. The doubled ending (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness ('a/some').
7.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to ooze, exude, or discharge; festering matter

1.meaning: He gulps it down little by little; he forces it down in repeated swallows, draining it with difficulty. The intensive verb form pictures a slow, laborious, distasteful drinking, sip after reluctant sip.
1.grammar: A present/future verb, third-person masculine singular ('he gulps it'), built on an intensive/reflexive pattern (the doubled middle root letter and ta- shaping) that conveys doing the act gradually and laboriously. The ya- prefix means 'he'; the -u on the stem marks the ongoing/indicative mood. The attached -hu means 'it/him' as the object.
1.root: ج-ر-ع (j-r-ʿ) — to swallow, gulp, drink down in mouthfuls

2.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
2.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

3.meaning: A present-tense verb 'it/he is almost (about to)'. It is a special 'verb of approach' meaning an action is on the verge of happening — nearly, but not quite, occurring.

parts.en: to be on the verge of (verb stem)

3.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he/it'; the stem is -kād-; the final -u is the separate indicative-mood ending. It normally governs a following present-tense verb, together meaning 'it almost (does) …'.
3.root: ك-و-د (k-w-d) — to be on the point of, almost do

4.meaning: He can(not) make it go down smoothly; he swallows it easily. The verb refers to letting something pass freely and palatably down the throat, the smooth, unforced act of swallowing.

parts.en: swallows smoothly / makes go down easily

4.grammar: A present/future verb, third-person masculine singular ('he makes it go down'), in the causative pattern (the yu- prefix plus the long internal vowel) meaning 'to cause to pass down easily.' The weak middle root letter surfaces as the long ī. The -u marks the ongoing/indicative mood; the attached -hu means 'it/him' as object.
4.root: س-و-غ (s-w-gh) — to be palatable, to go down easily, to swallow without difficulty

5.meaning: And it comes to him; it reaches him, approaches him, befalls him. The verb conveys something arriving at or coming upon a person.
5.grammar: A present/future verb, third-person masculine singular ('it/he comes'). The ya- prefix means 'he/it'; the final weak root letter appears as the long ī. The attached -hi means 'him / to him' as the one approached; its vowel is -hi (not -hu) because it follows the ī sound. The wa- prefix is 'and.'
5.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to arrive, to reach, to bring

6.meaning: Death — the ending of earthly life; the state or event of dying.
6.grammar: A definite noun ('al-' = 'the') with the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks it as the subject — the one doing or being something in the sentence.

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
8.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

9.meaning: A place, location, spot — the position or site where something is situated. The root relates to being established or located somewhere.
9.grammar: A noun (of place) with the ending -in: the -i is genitive (the case used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun, '… of/from a place'), and the final -n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a place').
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, come to be

10.meaning: A compound: the connective 'and' joined to the particle mā. The particle mā is highly versatile — it can mean 'what / whatever' (introducing an indirect question or a relative clause, 'that which'), or it can function as a negation ('not'). Context determines which sense applies; the core idea is an open, unspecified 'what(ever)' or a flat denial.
10.grammar: Two indeclinable particles, so there is no case ending to mark. The wa- prefix is the simple connective 'and', linking what follows to what precedes. Mā itself does not change form: it serves either as an interrogative/relative ('what, that which') or as a negating word ('not').

11.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
11.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

12.meaning: Dead; one who has died, a lifeless being. An adjective/noun describing that which has lost life, the opposite of living.
12.grammar: A singular adjective/noun on an intensive pattern (doubled middle letter) meaning 'dead.' It carries the -in ending, marking it indefinite ('a dead one / dead') and in the genitive case — the case required here by the preceding preposition bi- ('with/by'). The doubled -in (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness.
12.root: م-و-ت (m-w-t) — death, dying, lifelessness

13.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
13.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

14.meaning: From behind him / before him; on the far side of him. A spatial term built on a noun meaning 'the rear' or 'what lies beyond,' joined to a possessive 'his.' Idiomatically it can point either to what is behind a person or to what lies ahead awaiting him.
14.grammar: A noun of place meaning 'behind/beyond,' carrying the -i genitive ending because it is bound to the following possessor (literally 'the-behind OF him'). The attached -hi means 'his/him'; its vowel is -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows the -i sound. The wa- prefix is 'and.'
14.root: و-ر-ي (w-r-y) — to be behind, hidden, or beyond; the rear side

15.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
15.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

16.meaning: Coarse, harsh, rough, and severe; thick and unyielding. Used of texture it means 'rough,' and of character or treatment it means 'stern, hard, harsh.'
16.grammar: A singular adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern, meaning 'harsh/coarse.' The -un ending marks it as indefinite ('a harsh one / harsh') and in the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing simply being named. The doubled -un (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness.

1.meaning: A likeness, comparison, parable, or illustrative example; a similitude used to make something abstract vivid and understandable.
1.grammar: A singular noun with the -u (nominative) ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described. Being without tanwīn here, it commonly stands as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the likeness OF …').
1.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble; likeness, similitude, example

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: 'In/with their Lord' — combining the preposition 'bi' (with, in, by) and 'rabb', meaning the Lord, Master, Nurturer, and Sustainer who owns, governs, and brings to maturity all that He has created; with the attached pronoun 'their'.
4.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' attached to the noun 'rabb', which then carries the possessive pronoun '-him' ('their'). Because it follows the preposition, the noun takes the genitive '-i' vowel (heard in 'rabbi'); after a word ending in '-i', the pronoun is voiced 'him' rather than 'hum'.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, and lord over

5.meaning: Their deeds / works / actions — the things they have done.
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'deed', meaning 'deeds/works'. The attached -hum means 'their' (masculine plural), forming a possessive link. The -u before the pronoun is nominative, marking the whole phrase ('their deeds') as a subject. The -hum form keeps its u-vowel after this nominative ending.
5.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — working, doing, action

6.meaning: Like ashes; resembling the fine grey residue left after fire has consumed something. The word names burnt remains, here introduced by 'like' to make a comparison.
6.grammar: A singular noun meaning 'ashes,' preceded by the prefix ka- ('like/as'). It carries the -in ending, which here marks it indefinite ('ashes / some ashes') and in the genitive case — the case required after the comparative particle ka-. The doubled -in (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness.
6.root: ر-م-د (r-m-d) — ashes, the grey remains of fire

7.meaning: It blew violently; it raged and intensified. A verb describing a force, especially wind, that grows fierce and gathers strength.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person feminine singular ('she/it did'), on a reflexive/intensive pattern (the ish-ta- shaping with the doubled final root letter) meaning 'to grow intense, become severe.' The -t ending marks a feminine doer (fitting a grammatically feminine noun such as 'wind'). The completed -at signals a finished action.
7.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — strength, intensity, severity, becoming forceful

8.meaning: By it, with it, through it; the preposition 'bi' (with/by means of) joined to a pronoun referring to something previously mentioned.
8.grammar: A preposition plus an attached third-person masculine singular pronoun ('it / him'). 'Bi' conveys instrument or means ('by means of it'); the pronoun takes the -i vowel because words governed by 'bi' stand in the genitive.

9.meaning: The wind; moving air, a current of air. A common noun for the wind, with the definite article 'the.'
9.grammar: A singular (grammatically feminine) noun meaning 'wind,' made definite by the prefixed al- ('the'). The l of al- assimilates into the following r (so it is pronounced ar-rīḥ). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing simply being named.
9.root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ) — wind, breath, air, spirit

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
11.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
11.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

12.meaning: Stormy, raging, tempestuous; violently blowing. An adjective describing a day or wind marked by furious, gale-force turbulence.
12.grammar: A singular active participle (the ʿāʿiC 'doer' pattern) meaning 'stormy / blowing violently.' The -in ending marks it indefinite ('a stormy one / stormy') and in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or when one noun is linked to another ('… of …'). The doubled -in (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness.
12.root: ع-ص-ف (ʿ-ṣ-f) — to blow violently, to storm, to rage (of wind)

13.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
13.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

14.meaning: They are able, they have power over, or they have control — to be capable of doing or disposing of something.
14.grammar: Present/future tense verb. The 'ya-...-ūna' frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the final '-na' marks the indicative mood — a plain statement that the action holds true.
14.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — power, ability, capacity, measure

15.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
15.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

16.meaning: 'They earned / they acquired / they gained' — past-tense action of a group obtaining something through their own effort, whether good or bad. The root carries the sense of working to acquire, and is often used of the deeds people accrue.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -ū marks a masculine plural subject ('they') who completed the action in the past.

17.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
17.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

18.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
18.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

19.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
19.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

20.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
20.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

21.meaning: The straying / error / being lost — wandering off the right path; a noun naming the state of having gone astray, made definite by 'the.'
21.grammar: A noun with al- ('the'); the l assimilates into the following 'ḍ' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced aḍ-ḍalāl. The final -u marks the nominative, the case used for a subject or predicate. It names the abstract condition of straying from truth or guidance.
21.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, be lost, err

22.meaning: The far, the distant, the remote. An adjective describing that which is a long way off in place, time, or degree; the definite 'the' makes it specific.
22.grammar: A singular adjective on the faʿīl pattern, meaning 'far/distant,' made definite by the prefixed al- ('the'). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing simply being named.

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
3.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
4.root: — (proper name)

5.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
5.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.
5.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — creating, originating, shaping

6.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
6.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

7.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, or the planet earth; the world we stand upon, often paired with the heavens to mean all of creation.
7.grammar: A feminine noun, prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed by certain particles.

8.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
8.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
8.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

9.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
9.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'He wills, wishes, or so chooses' — to want and intend something by sovereign decision. The root denotes willing and desiring as an act of the will.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'). This is a hollow verb (the weak letter sits in the middle of the root, with hamza as the strong final radical). In the jussive/conditional mood the medial long vowel is shortened (giving 'yashaʾ' rather than 'yashāʾ') — the form taken after 'if' or in a conditional clause.

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'He takes you (plural) away,' 'He causes you to depart,' or 'He does away with you' — to remove or make something go. It carries an attached object 'you all.'
11.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'), in the causative pattern ('to make go / take away'), with the attached object -kum ('you all'). The unvowelled final stem consonant marks the jussive/conditional mood, as in the answer to an 'if.'
11.root: ذ-ه-ب (dh-h-b) — going, departing, taking away

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'and He brings, comes with, or produces' — to come bearing something, hence to bring it forth. It joins to what precedes with a connective 'and.'
12.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'), prefixed with 'and.' The final weak letter is trimmed, marking the jussive/conditional mood — the form taken in the answer to a condition or after 'if.'
12.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming, arriving, bringing

13.meaning: A creation; a created thing, a brought-into-being entity, a making. The word denotes both the act of creating and the creature or formation that results.
13.grammar: A singular verbal noun meaning 'creation / a created thing,' preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/of'). The -in ending marks it indefinite ('a creation') and in the genitive case — the case required here by the preceding preposition bi-. The doubled -in (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness.
13.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, fashion, bring into being

14.meaning: New, fresh, recently brought into being; novel. An adjective describing something newly made, as opposed to old or worn.
14.grammar: A singular adjective on the faʿīl pattern, meaning 'new/fresh.' The -in ending marks it indefinite ('a new one / new') and in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun ('… of …'). The doubled -in (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness. The -in here mirrors the case of the noun it describes.
14.root: ج-د-د (j-d-d) — newness, freshness, renewal

1.meaning: A compound: the connective 'and' joined to the particle mā. The particle mā is highly versatile — it can mean 'what / whatever' (introducing an indirect question or a relative clause, 'that which'), or it can function as a negation ('not'). Context determines which sense applies; the core idea is an open, unspecified 'what(ever)' or a flat denial.
1.grammar: Two indeclinable particles, so there is no case ending to mark. The wa- prefix is the simple connective 'and', linking what follows to what precedes. Mā itself does not change form: it serves either as an interrogative/relative ('what, that which') or as a negating word ('not').

2.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
2.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

3.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
3.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
3.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'Mighty / strong / dear' — one who is powerful and unassailable, hard to overcome and highly esteemed. The faʿīl pattern gives an intensive, enduring sense.
5.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to an intensive adjective. The final -in is the indefinite genitive ending, which a noun takes after a preposition; the genitive is the case that typically follows prepositions or links a word to a preceding one.
5.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, being unassailable and honoured

1.meaning: And they came forth / went out into the open; they emerged into plain view, became prominent or exposed. The verb conveys stepping out into visibility from concealment.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they did'). The -ū ending is the subject marker 'they' for a group of males (or mixed group); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention. The completed form signals a finished action. The wa- prefix is 'and.'
1.root: ب-ر-ز (b-r-z) — to come out, emerge, appear prominently, stand forth

2.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
2.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

3.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
