4.meaning: The ritual Prayer — the formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. More broadly the root conveys connection, supplication, and reaching out to the divine; it is the central act of Islamic devotion.
4.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the prayer'). The article al- means 'the.' The -i ending (on the feminine tā') is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to another noun in an 'of' relationship (e.g. 'of the prayer / to the prayer').
4.root: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w) — prayer, worship, connection, supplication

5.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
5.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

6.meaning: Offspring, progeny, descendants — the line of children and their children that issue from a person; collective in sense, covering one's seed and posterity.
6.grammar: A feminine noun carrying a collective meaning ('descendants'). The attached -ī is the first-person possessive pronoun, 'my,' giving 'my offspring.' Before such a possessive, the noun takes the genitive vowel -i, the case that typically signals possession or links the word to what follows.
6.root: ذ-ر-ر / ذ-ر-أ (dh-r-r / dh-r-ʾ) — to scatter, multiply, bring forth

7.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

7.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

8.meaning: To accept favorably and with approval; to receive (a deed, prayer, or repentance) graciously and grant it acceptance — more than mere taking, it implies welcoming with good pleasure.
8.grammar: A command (imperative) verb on the intensive Form V pattern, which adds the nuance of accepting willingly and with favor. The bare, vowelless ending is the masculine singular imperative addressed to one person ('you, accept!'). The prefixed wa- means 'and,' joining it to what precedes.
8.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to accept, receive, face toward

9.meaning: A call, supplication, or invocation; the act of calling upon Allah in entreaty, prayer, or petition.
9.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action 'calling / supplicating'). The final -i is the genitive ending, the case that usually marks possession, links the word to a following noun ('… of …'), or follows a preposition. Here the genitive is produced by a construct (iḍāfa) link to a following possessor; the -i is purely the case vowel and does not itself encode any pronoun. When a first-person possessor ('my') is understood, that meaning comes from a possessive yāʾ that has been elided, not from the genitive vowel.
9.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke

1.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

1.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

2.meaning: Forgive! — a plea or command to pardon, to cover over and blot out wrongdoing. It carries the sense of veiling a fault so it is no longer held against the offender.
2.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person: 'forgive!'. The vowelless final -r reflects the imperative form. It is commonly followed by 'us' or 'for me' to specify whom to pardon.
2.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and pardon; mercy that blots out sin

3.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
3.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

4.meaning: Parents — the two who gave one birth, father and mother taken together as a pair.
4.grammar: A dual noun ('the two parents') carrying the possessive 'my.' It follows the preposition li- ('for / to'). The dual ending appears in its genitive form -ay (rather than -ā), which is the shape duals take after a preposition or in a possession link; the attached -ya is 'my,' so the whole means 'and for my two parents.'
4.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to beget, give birth

5.meaning: Believers — those who have faith, who inwardly affirm and trust in Allah and give security through that faith; the ones characterized by true belief.
5.grammar: A masculine sound plural active participle ('those who believe'), built on the causative Form IV pattern (faith that brings about inner security/affirmation). The plural ending -īna is the form used for the object of a verb or after a preposition; here it follows li- ('for'), and the prefixed al- ('the') makes it definite — 'and for the believers.'
5.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, faith, trust

6.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
6.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
6.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

7.meaning: He stands up, rises, or gets to his feet; also to undertake or attend to a matter. The core image is of coming to an upright, established position.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u marks the indicative mood, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('he stands / he is standing'); a change of that final vowel would signal a different mood.

8.meaning: The reckoning, the accounting, the settling of accounts; a careful computing and calling-to-account, as when deeds are tallied and judged.
8.grammar: A verbal noun ('the act of reckoning / accounting'), made definite by al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: Do (not) suppose / reckon / imagine — to think something to be the case, to deem or assume (often a mistaken estimation).
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The heavy '-anna' ending is the emphatic ('nūn of emphasis'), strengthening the verb — typically attached after a command or prohibition ('do not ever suppose…').
2.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, count, suppose, estimate

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: Heedless, inattentive, unaware; one who is absent-minded and neglectful, failing to notice or take account of something.
4.grammar: An active participle ('one who is heedless') on the basic Form I pattern. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (the doubled-fatḥa 'tanwīn'), which marks an indefinite word as a direct object, or very often as a descriptive 'state' word telling how or in what condition someone is ('… being heedless').
4.root: غ-ف-ل (gh-f-l) — to be heedless, neglectful, inattentive

5.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
5.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

6.meaning: To do, to work, to act; to carry out a deed or perform an action, whether good or bad.
6.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb on the basic Form I pattern. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he / it does'). The final -u is the indicative ending, the default mood used for a plain, ongoing or habitual statement of fact.

7.meaning: Wrongdoers — those who commit injustice, who put things out of their right place and transgress against truth, others, or their own souls; oppressors.
7.grammar: A masculine sound plural active participle ('those who do wrong'), made definite by al- ('the'). The plural ending -ūna is the nominative form, used when the plural is the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.
7.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress, put in the wrong place

8.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
8.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

9.meaning: To defer, postpone, or grant a delay to them; to put them off to a later time rather than seizing them at once — implying respite or reprieve.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb on the intensive Form II pattern ('to put off, delay'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he defers'). The base vowel before the suffix is the indicative -u (plain statement of fact). The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them,' giving 'he defers them / grants them delay.'
9.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be later, to come behind, to defer

10.meaning: For a day; toward a day. The noun yawm means 'day' — a defined period or appointed time, often a momentous occasion. With the prefixed particle it means 'for / to / on a day', pointing toward an appointed time.
10.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition li- ('for, to'). Because it follows a preposition, it takes the -i (genitive) ending, here with tanwīn (the doubled-n sound) marking it indefinite: '-in' = 'for a day'. The genitive is the case regularly required after prepositions.
10.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

11.meaning: To stare fixedly and wide open, with an unblinking, transfixed gaze; (of eyes) to be wide and staring, as in terror or shock.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb on the basic Form I pattern. The ta- prefix here marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she / it stares') — the form used with feminine subjects such as 'eyes.' The final -u is the indicative ending, the default mood for a plain factual statement.
11.root: ش-خ-ص (sh-kh-ṣ) — to fix the gaze, stare; to rise/be prominent

12.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
12.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

13.meaning: The eyes; the seeing faculties or sights — the organs of vision (a plural of 'baṣar,' eyesight).
13.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun meaning 'eyes / faculties of sight,' made definite by al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.
13.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, perceive, have sight/insight

1.meaning: Rushing forward with necks outstretched, hastening eagerly with heads raised; those who hurry headlong toward something, eyes fixed ahead.
1.grammar: A masculine sound plural active participle on the causative Form IV pattern, describing people 'hastening forward with outstretched necks.' The plural ending -īna is the form used for the object of a verb or, very commonly, as a descriptive 'state' word telling how a group is — here, 'rushing forward.'
1.root: ه-ط-ع (h-ṭ-ʿ) — to hasten with the gaze/neck fixed forward

2.meaning: Holding the heads up and back with a fixed stare; those craning their necks upward, faces lifted and frozen — a posture of stricken gazing.
2.grammar: A masculine sound plural active participle on the causative Form IV pattern, describing those 'raising / craning their heads.' Its plural would normally end in -īna, but here it appears as -ī because the final nūn is dropped when the participle is joined to a following noun it governs (a construct/'iḍāfa' link) — typically 'raisers of (their heads).'
2.root: ق-ن-ع (q-n-ʿ) — to raise the head, lift up; also to be content

3.meaning: Their heads; the topmost part of the body, here belonging to a group of males ('their heads').
3.grammar: A plural noun (raʾs 'head' → ruʾūs 'heads') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case (after a preposition or in a possessive link). The suffix -him means 'their,' referring to a group of males; its vowel is -him because it follows an -i sound.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: To come back, return, or revert; (of a glance) to bounce back to a person — used of something that recoils or fails to settle.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb on the reflexive Form VIII pattern ('to turn back upon oneself, revert'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('it returns'). The final -u is the indicative ending, the default mood for a plain factual statement; the doubled dāl reflects the merging of the root's repeated consonant.
5.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, send back, repel

6.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
6.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
6.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: The blink or glance of the eye; the swift movement of the eyelid or the gaze itself — the look of the eyes (here possessed: 'their glance').
7.grammar: A noun meaning 'the glance / the blink of the eye,' with the attached possessive -hum ('their'), giving 'their glance.' The base vowel -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.

8.meaning: The hearts — understood as the inner seat of feeling, understanding, and resolve; the innermost cores or minds (a plural of 'fuʾād').
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun meaning 'hearts / inner cores,' with the attached possessive -hum ('their'), giving 'their hearts.' The base vowel -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the subject or the thing being described. The prefixed wa- means 'and.'
8.root: ف-ء-د (f-ʾ-d) — the heart; to be stirred/inflamed within

9.meaning: Empty air, void, vacancy; literally 'air,' used figuratively of something hollow and emptied out — devoid of content or sense.
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'air / empty space.' The ending -un is the indefinite nominative (the doubled-ḍamma 'tanwīn'), which marks an indefinite word that serves as the subject or, often, as the description/predicate of a sentence ('… is empty void').
9.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — air, empty space; to fall, to incline/desire

1.meaning: To warn; to give notice of impending danger or consequence so that the hearer may take heed and beware — a cautioning meant to rouse vigilance.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb on the causative Form IV pattern ('to make aware of danger, to warn'). It is addressed to one person ('you, warn!'). The base form ends without a vowel; the small -i shown here is a 'helping vowel' added only to smooth the join with a following word, not a case or mood ending. The prefixed wa- means 'and.'
1.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution; a vow/solemn notice

2.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
2.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
2.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

3.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
3.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
3.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

4.meaning: To come to them, to reach or arrive upon them; the approach of something that befalls or overtakes people.

parts.en: final weak root letter (yāʾ) of the stem

4.grammar: A present-tense verb on the basic Form I pattern ('to come') from the defective root ء-ت-ي. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he / it comes'). The yāʾ with its kasra (-ī) is the third and final root letter of this weak-lām root, an intrinsic part of the verb's stem — not an inserted helping or linking vowel. The attached -him is the object pronoun 'them' (its vowel raised to -himu to ease the join with a following word), giving 'it comes to them.'
4.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring

5.meaning: "the punishment / torment" — a painful penalty or chastisement inflicted as retribution; suffering imposed as a consequence.
5.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a verb or the doer/topic of a sentence.
5.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment

6.meaning: Then/so He says — the verb 'say' joined to a connector meaning 'then' or 'so,' indicating a statement that follows as a consequence.
6.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb prefixed by 'then/so.' The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he.' The final -u ending is the indicative mood, signalling a plain statement of fact.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
8.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

9.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

9.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

10.meaning: Defer us, grant us delay, put us off (to a later term); a plea to be given more time rather than be taken now.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) verb on the intensive Form II pattern ('to put off, postpone'), addressed to one person ('you, defer!'). The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us,' giving 'grant us delay / defer us.'
10.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be later, to come behind, to defer

11.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
11.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'a fixed term, an appointed time, a set deadline, a span allotted before something falls due.' It denotes the limit or end-point of a period.
12.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a term'). This form occurs after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun.
12.root: ا-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed time, deadline

13.meaning: 'Near / soon / close' — qarīb denotes nearness in place or time, hence 'close at hand' or 'shortly,' or one who is near/related.
13.grammar: An adjective/noun on the fa'īl pattern meaning 'near.' The -in ending is the genitive case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' the form taken after a preposition or in an 'of …' relationship with a preceding noun.
13.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, draw close; nearness

14.meaning: To respond, answer, or comply; to give a positive response to a call or request — used of answering a summons or granting a petition.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb on the causative Form IV pattern ('to give an answer, to respond'). The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we answer'). The bare, vowelless ending (here on 'jib') is the jussive/conditional mood, the clipped form a verb takes after certain particles or as the 'then'-clause of a condition ('… we would answer').
14.root: ج-و-ب (j-w-b) — to answer, respond; to traverse

15.meaning: Your call, your summons, your invitation; the act of calling or inviting, here directed from or belonging to the one addressed ('your calling').
15.grammar: A verbal noun ('the act of calling / a summons') with the attached possessive -ka ('your,' addressing one male), giving 'your call.' The base vowel -a is the accusative ending, the case that typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

16.meaning: And we follow / we will follow — to walk behind someone, take them as a guide, pursue or obey a path, person, or teaching.
16.grammar: Present-tense verb in Form VIII (taking on / pursuing for oneself). The na- prefix means 'we'. This is a sound (non-defective) verb, so its jussive mood would be marked by sukun (no vowel) on the final consonant. The final -i is therefore NOT a mood ending: it is an epenthetic (helping) vowel inserted to break up a cluster of two unvowelled consonants where the verb meets a following word that begins with a consonant cluster (iltiqāʾ al-sākinayn). The mood itself remains jussive.
16.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, succeed

17.meaning: The messengers / the envoys — the plural of 'messenger,' those sent with a message; in religious usage, the prophets sent by Allah.
17.grammar: A plural noun made definite by 'the.' The final -a is the accusative case, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb (the one acted upon). The doubled r- shows the 'l' of 'the' assimilating into the following sound.
17.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, a messenger

18.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
18.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').

19.meaning: You (plural) are / you happen to be. A form of the 'hollow' verb kāna ('to be'), which links a subject to a state or description, or expresses simply being or existing.
19.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The dropping of the usual final -na (so takūnū rather than takūnūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form expected after conditional or subordinating particles.
19.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

20.meaning: You swore / took an oath: a completed-action verb of solemnly vowing or asserting under oath. The Form IV pattern gives the sense of binding oneself by a sworn declaration.
20.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in Form IV. The -tum ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all swore'). Form IV here conveys the act of taking a binding oath.
20.root: ق-س-م (q-s-m) — to swear an oath; also to divide, apportion

21.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
21.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

22.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
22.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
22.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

23.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
23.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

24.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
24.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

25.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
25.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

26.meaning: A ceasing, passing away, decline, or coming to an end — the vanishing of something that once existed, the point at which a thing is no more.
26.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'cessation' or 'decline'. The -in ending is indefinite genitive (tanwīn al-kasr): it marks the word as 'a ___' (unspecified) and typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
26.root: ز-و-ل (z-w-l) — to cease, pass away, decline, shift away

1.meaning: And you dwelt / settled — to take up residence, abide, and find rest in a place; to live somewhere as one's home.
1.grammar: Past-tense verb. The suffix -tum means 'you (all)' did the action — a completed act of dwelling by a group addressed directly. The root sense pairs settling-in-place with calm and rest.
1.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to dwell, be still, find rest

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
2.root: — (particle)

3.meaning: Dwellings, residences, abodes — the places in which people live and settle.
3.grammar: A plural noun of place ('places of dwelling'). It follows the diptote pattern (mafāʿil), so its definite/construct genitive takes a single -i rather than -in. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the dwellings OF …') or follows a preposition.
3.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to dwell, be still, find rest

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
5.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
6.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

7.meaning: And it became clear / evident — for something to be made plain, distinct, and unmistakable, so that the truth of it shows itself.
7.grammar: Past-tense verb in Form V (tafaʿʿala), here carrying the sense of something gradually becoming or showing itself clearly. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for 'he/it' (third-person masculine singular): a completed action, 'it became clear'.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct, evident; separation

8.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

9.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
9.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.
9.root: — (interrogative particle; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: We did / We dealt / We acted — to carry out, perform, or do something; the most general verb for performing an action.
10.grammar: Past-tense verb. The suffix -nā means 'we' performed the action — a completed deed done by the speaker(s). This is the base verb 'to do', from which Arabic grammarians take their model for all verb patterns.

11.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
11.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

12.meaning: And We struck / set forth / put forward — literally 'to strike', but very commonly 'to set down' or 'present' something such as an example, likeness, or saying.
12.grammar: Past-tense verb. The suffix -nā means 'we' did the action — a completed act. The root's core meaning is 'to strike', which extends idiomatically to 'putting forth' or 'coining' an example or parable.
12.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike, beat; to set forth (an example)

13.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
13.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

14.meaning: The likenesses / parables / examples — the plural of mathal, a comparison, similitude, or illustrative example used to make a truth vivid. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the examples').
14.grammar: A definite plural noun (with al-). The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
14.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similitude, example

1.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
1.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

2.meaning: They plotted / schemed — to devise a hidden plan or stratagem against someone, working secretly to bring about an outcome.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb. The ending -ū means 'they (all)' did the action — a completed act of scheming by a group. (The written alif after the wāw is silent.) The root denotes covert planning, which may be blameworthy or, when ascribed to Allah, a just outmaneuvering of such plots.
2.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to plot, scheme, devise a stratagem

3.meaning: Their plot / scheme — a contrived secret plan or stratagem belonging to them.
3.grammar: A verbal noun ('plotting') with the attached pronoun -hum meaning 'their'. The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing being done or carried out).
3.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to plot, scheme, devise a stratagem

4.meaning: The compound 'and with / and in the presence of' — the connector 'and' joined to a word meaning 'with, near, in the presence of, in the sight of'. This locational/possessive term points to something being held, present, or reckoned in someone's estimation.

parts.en: with, near, in the presence of

4.grammar: The connective 'and' (wa-) prefixed to the locational word ʿinda. ʿinda is an adverb of place/possession ('with, at, in the presence of') that always stands in the accusative-looking form ending in -a and is followed by a noun or pronoun it relates to, giving 'with/in the sight of …'.
4.root: — (no triliteral verbal root; ʿinda is a locational particle)

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: Scheming, plotting, or covert stratagem — a cunning plan, often devised in secret. With the suffix it means 'their plotting / their scheme'.
6.grammar: A noun carrying the -u (nominative) ending, the form typically used when the word is the subject of a sentence. The attached -hum ('their') makes it possessive: 'their plot'.
6.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to scheme, devise a crafty plan

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
7.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

8.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

8.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

9.meaning: Scheming, plotting, or covert stratagem — a cunning plan, often devised in secret. With the suffix it means 'their plotting / their scheme'.
9.grammar: A noun carrying the -u (nominative) ending, the form typically used when the word is the subject of a sentence. The attached -hum ('their') makes it possessive: 'their plot'.
9.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — to scheme, devise a crafty plan

10.meaning: That … should pass away / be removed / disappear — for something to cease to exist, be shifted out of place, or come to an end.
10.grammar: Present-tense verb with the prefix li- ('so that / in order to'). The ta- prefix here marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she'). Because li- introduces purpose, the verb is in the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a ('so that it should pass away').
10.root: ز-و-ل (z-w-l) — to cease, pass away, decline, shift away

11.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
11.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
11.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

12.meaning: The mountains — the great, firmly rooted masses of rock and earth, often evoked as images of immovable solidity.
12.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, 'mountains', made definite by al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject or doer — the one the sentence is about.
12.root: ج-ب-ل (j-b-l) — mountain, that which is firmly fixed

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

2.meaning: Do (not) suppose / reckon / imagine — to think something to be the case, to deem or assume (often a mistaken estimation).
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The heavy '-anna' ending is the emphatic ('nūn of emphasis'), strengthening the verb — typically attached after a command or prohibition ('do not ever suppose…').
2.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, count, suppose, estimate

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: One who breaks / fails to keep — a breaker of a promise or appointment; one who goes back on what was pledged.

parts.en: breaker (of a promise) — Form IV active participle

4.grammar: An active participle from Form IV (afʿala), naming the doer: 'one who fails to keep / breaks (a pledge)'. The -a ending is accusative — the case often used for the predicate after negation or as a direct object — describing the one characterized by this breaking.
4.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to be behind, succeed; to break / go back on (a pledge)

5.meaning: His promise / pledge — a firm undertaking or commitment to do (or threat to do) something, here belonging to 'Him'.
5.grammar: A verbal noun ('a promising') with the attached pronoun -hi meaning 'his'. The -i ending is genitive: it marks the noun as the possessed thing in a possessive relationship ('the promise OF Him'), and the pronoun shifts to -hi (with long vowel hī) after that -i.
5.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give one's word

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'His messengers / His envoys' — the plural of 'messenger' (one sent with a commission) with an attached pronoun 'His.'
6.grammar: A plural noun in a possessive construction with the pronoun 'His' (-hu). The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('…disobeyed His messengers'). 'Rusul' is the broken (irregular) plural of rasūl.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a sent one, messenger

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
9.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").
9.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, honour, strength

10.meaning: Owner of / possessor of / endowed with — a word that does not stand alone but means 'the one who has' whatever noun follows it, ascribing that quality or possession to someone.

parts.en: possessor of, owner of, endowed with

10.grammar: A possessive noun meaning 'owner/possessor of', always followed by another noun in the genitive. The final -ū form here is the nominative case, used when this word names the subject or is the thing being described; it inherently requires a following noun to complete its sense ('owner OF …').
10.root: — (no triliteral root; an irregular noun of possession)

11.meaning: Retribution, vengeance, or requital — the act of repaying wrongdoing with deserved punishment.
11.grammar: A verbal noun (Form VIII, the name of the action 'taking retribution'). The -in ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the genitive case, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
11.root: ن-ق-م (n-q-m) — to take vengeance, exact retribution

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

2.meaning: It is changed / replaced / substituted — for one thing to be exchanged for another, altered, or swapped out.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb in the passive voice (Form II, baddala = to exchange). The vowelling tu-…-a-…-u marks 'is being changed' with an unnamed agent; the ta- prefix indicates a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement.
2.root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l) — to change, exchange, substitute, replace

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'the earth', 'the ground', or 'the land' — the terrestrial world, the soil and land surface as opposed to the sky.
3.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action). This noun is grammatically feminine.

4.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
4.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
4.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

5.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
5.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

6.meaning: And the heavens — the skies and all the celestial realms above; the visible heaven and the unseen heavens together.
6.grammar: A sound feminine plural of samāʾ ('heaven, sky') with the definite article al-. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence (the doer or the thing spoken about). The l of al- assimilates into the following s (a 'sun letter'), so it is pronounced as-samāwāt.
6.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; the sky / heaven

7.meaning: And they came forth / went out into the open; they emerged into plain view, became prominent or exposed. The verb conveys stepping out into visibility from concealment.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they did'). The -ū ending is the subject marker 'they' for a group of males (or mixed group); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention. The completed form signals a finished action. The wa- prefix is 'and.'
7.root: ب-ر-ز (b-r-z) — to come out, emerge, appear prominently, stand forth

8.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
8.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

9.meaning: The One — the single, unique One; absolutely one without partner, division, or equal. A divine name conveying sole, indivisible oneness.
9.grammar: A descriptive noun ('the One') with the definite article al-. The -i ending is genitive: it typically appears when the word follows a preposition or describes/agrees with another noun that is itself genitive. As a divine attribute it affirms Allah's absolute uniqueness.
9.root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d) — to be one, single, unique, alone

10.meaning: The Subduer / the Irresistible — the One whose overwhelming power dominates and prevails over all, so that nothing can withstand or escape Him. A divine name of total, conquering might.
10.grammar: An intensive form (faʿʿāl, denoting constant, overwhelming degree) meaning 'the One who utterly subdues', with the definite article al-. The -i ending is genitive: it typically appears after a preposition or in agreement with another genitive noun. As a divine name it stresses irresistible, all-conquering dominance over all creation.
10.root: ق-ه-ر (q-h-r) — to overpower, subdue, dominate, vanquish

1.meaning: "and you see / would see" — to perceive with the eyes or to behold; also "to regard" something as being a certain way.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb in the second-person masculine singular: the ta- prefix means "you (one man)." This verb comes from a weak root, so its final weak letter shows as the long -ā vowel; in the indicative it expresses ongoing or potential seeing.
1.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, behold

2.meaning: Those who commit grave sins and crimes; wrongdoers who deliberately break Allah's law and cut themselves off in guilt. The word denotes hardened, culpable offenders, not those who err by accident.
2.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) of Form IV, made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case, so it names a group as the object of a verb or the complement of a preposition, rather than the subject.
2.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime or grave sin

3.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
3.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

4.meaning: Bound / coupled / shackled together — joined and fastened to one another, linked closely as if chained side by side.
4.grammar: A passive participle in the sound masculine plural, from Form II (qarrana = to couple/yoke together): 'ones who have been bound together'. The ending -īna is the accusative/genitive form of the masculine plural, typically marking such a group as a direct object or as the subject of a circumstantial description ('being shackled together').
4.root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n) — to join, couple, yoke, link together

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: Fetters / shackles / chains — the iron bonds used to bind and restrain captives.
6.grammar: A plural noun ('bonds, fetters') with the definite article al-. The -i ending is genitive: it typically appears when the word follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

1.meaning: Their garments / shirts — the long shirts or robes worn on the body; coverings clothing them.
1.grammar: A plural noun ('shirts, garments') with the attached pronoun -hum ('their'). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence (the thing spoken about) — 'their garments' as the topic.
1.root: س-ر-ب-ل (s-r-b-l) — to clothe; (quadriliteral) a shirt / garment

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

3.meaning: Tar / pitch / liquid bitumen — a black, sticky, flammable substance.
3.grammar: A noun naming the substance 'tar/pitch'. The -in ending is indefinite genitive (tanwīn al-kasr): it marks the word as 'some ___' (unspecified) and typically appears when the noun is linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship or follows a preposition.
3.root: ق-ط-ر (q-ṭ-r) — to drip, flow in drops; (related) tar / pitch

4.meaning: And it covers / overwhelms / envelops — to come over something and engulf it completely, so it is wrapped up and overspread.

parts.en: covers / envelops (present-tense verb, weak final root)

4.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she covers'). Because the root ends in a weak letter, the ending appears as a long -ā (written with alif maqṣūra) rather than a short vowel; the sense is an ongoing or impending overwhelming.
4.root: غ-ش-ي (gh-sh-y) — to cover, envelop, overwhelm, come over

5.meaning: Their faces — the faces belonging to them; by extension, what faces forward or the very persons themselves.
5.grammar: A plural noun ('faces') with the attached pronoun 'their'. The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon). The pronoun is here vowelled -humu (rather than -hum) to ease pronunciation before a following word.
5.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face; direction, aspect, that which faces

6.meaning: The Fire — a definite noun for fire; frequently the term for the blazing punishment of the Hereafter (Hell).
6.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

1.meaning: '...so that He may reward/requite' — to give due recompense, repaying a person according to their deeds, whether good or ill.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he requites'), preceded by 'li-' meaning 'so that / in order that', which expresses purpose. Because of this particle the verb takes the subjunctive mood, shown by the final '-a' (here '-ya' on the weak-ending verb) instead of the usual '-u' — marking an intended or hoped-for outcome rather than a plain fact. It typically takes an object: the one being recompensed.
1.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — recompense, requital, reward

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
3.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'soul, self, person, living being.' It denotes the inner self or the whole individual — the seat of life and identity, and by extension a 'person' as a single unit.
4.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a soul'). This form appears after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun (such as 'every soul').
4.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being

5.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
5.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
5.root: — (particle; no root)

6.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
6.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
6.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: Swift, quick, fast — describing one who is rapid in carrying out something. Used of Allah, it conveys that an action (such as reckoning) is accomplished with utter speed.
9.grammar: An adjective in the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (denoting a strong, inherent quality). The final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case; with no tanwīn here it is in a possessive construction, 'swift of …,' linking it to a following noun.
9.root: س-ر-ع (s-r-ʿ) — to be swift, quick

10.meaning: The reckoning, accounting, or calling to account — the tallying and settling of deeds; also calculation or counting in a general sense.
10.grammar: A definite verbal noun with the article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i (kasra) marks the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or as the second part of a possessive pair ('… of the reckoning').

1.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

2.meaning: A conveying / a notification / a sufficient message — the act and content of delivering communication so it reaches and informs its hearers; that which is enough to make the point.
2.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'a conveying / proclamation that reaches its hearers'. The -un ending is indefinite nominative (tanwīn al-ḍamm): it marks the word as 'a ___' (unspecified) and as the subject or predicate of a sentence (the thing spoken about).
2.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, arrive at, attain; to convey

3.meaning: For the people, for mankind, for humankind. The preposition 'for/to' joined to 'the people' as a collective term for human beings.
3.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') prefixed to the noun 'al-nās' ('the people'). The article 'al-' loses its 'a' sound after 'li-' and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's initial n (hence the doubled 'nn'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition.

4.meaning: And so that they may be warned — that they be cautioned and put on guard against a danger or consequence yet to come.

parts.en: they are warned (Form IV passive stem)

4.grammar: Present-tense verb in the passive voice (Form IV, andhara = to warn), with the prefix li- ('so that / in order that'). The present-tense prefix carries a ḍamma — yu- — which (together with the fatḥa on the consonant before the last root letter) marks the passive voice, giving 'they are warned' by an unnamed warner. Because li- expresses purpose, the verb is subjunctive, shown by the plural ending -ū (the indicative's final nūn is dropped; the written alif is silent).
4.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution, give notice of danger

5.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

6.meaning: And so that they may know / come to realize. The word expresses purpose: an outcome of knowing, recognizing, or becoming aware is intended, attributed to a group of male (or mixed) people. The opening element conveys 'and,' while the attached purpose-particle frames what follows as the goal or intended result of an action.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb placed in the subjunctive after the purpose-particle li- ('so that'). The ya- prefix marks third-person, and the -ū ending marks a masculine-plural subject ('they'); the normal final -na of such verbs is dropped because the subjunctive particle governs it, which is why it reads -ū rather than -ūna. The whole signals an intended purpose or outcome: 'so that they may know.'

7.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that …' or 'only that' — it introduces and emphasizes a fact as the content of a thought or statement; 'anna' asserts ('indeed/that') and the attached 'mā' often gives a restrictive sense ('that … is only …').
7.grammar: A combination of the emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with 'mā'. 'Anna' introduces a noun-clause as the object of verbs like 'think' or 'know', putting the following noun in the accusative. Joined with 'mā' it frequently carries a limiting force, 'only/merely'. Particles like this do not themselves take case endings.

8.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
8.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

9.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
9.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
9.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

10.meaning: One / single and unique — denoting oneness: a single individual, undivided and without partner or plurality.
10.grammar: An adjective/numeral meaning 'one.' The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, the case typically used for a subject, predicate, or a descriptor agreeing with such a noun.

11.meaning: And so that one may take heed / call to mind / reflect. It expresses purpose: the intended outcome is that a single male party should remind himself, recall, and bear a lesson in mind. This is a Form V (tafaʿʿala) verb, which is active and reflexive — the subject does the remembering to and for himself — carrying the sense of deliberately letting something sink in.

parts.en: remind oneself / take heed (Form V, active-reflexive)

11.grammar: A present-tense Form V verb (tafaʿʿala / yatafaʿʿalu) in the subjunctive after the purpose-particle li- ('so that'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he / one'). The form shows TWO separate doublings: (1) the doubled ذّ arises from assimilation — the underlying Form V prefix tā' (yataḏakkar) merges into the following root letter ذ, producing yaḏḏakkar; (2) the doubled كّ is the gemination of the middle root letter that is built into the Form V (faʿʿala) template itself. Form V is active-reflexive, so the meaning is 'to remind oneself / take heed,' not a passive 'be reminded.' The final -a is the subjunctive ending triggered by li-, marking purpose: 'so that one may take heed.'
11.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

12.meaning: 'Possessors of / owners of / people of' — a plural construct word meaning those endowed with or characterized by whatever follows it (e.g. 'those of understanding'). It has no singular of its own form and is always joined to a following noun.
12.grammar: A masculine plural noun used only in the construct state (always followed by another noun, 'possessors OF ...'). The -ū ending is the nominative plural form, marking it as the subject or doer of a sentence. The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
12.root: — (a word for 'possessors of', having no verbal root)

13.meaning: The inner cores / kernels — figuratively, sound minds, understanding, or insight. Literally the plural of 'lubb,' the kernel or pith inside a shell; used of the discerning faculty of the heart, so 'people of the albāb' are those of genuine understanding and reflection.

parts.en: kernels / minds, understanding (broken plural of lubb)

13.grammar: A definite plural noun. The first segment الۡ (al-) is the definite article 'the.' Note that the word that follows already begins with its own alif-hamza: it is ʾalbāb, the broken (irregular) plural of lubb formed on the ʾafʿāl pattern, where that initial alif belongs to the plural template itself and is NOT a second definite article. So there is only one article here, prefixed to the intrinsic ʾalbāb. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition or governing particle.
13.root: ل-ب-ب (l-b-b) — core, kernel, inner essence; hence sound intellect
